rationale: Hold, as Sunday's proposal said it would: Tuesday's 10 km was the calf test, and the calf was felt the whole way ("like a bruise", easing a little after 5 km). That is the wrong direction — on 11 Nov it came in the last km, on 14 Nov it faded to nothing, and now it is there from the start — and your physio now thinks it is a strain, not overload. A strain heals on its own timescale, and running on it at 1/10 keeps it irritated, which is why three weeks of easing back have not cleared it. So: no running until it is 0/10 — not 1 — on walking, stairs, single-leg calf raises and hops for three days, and your physio has cleared you. Bike for the aerobic work (seated, normal cadence) and her calf loading in the gym. The next two weeks are a provisional return: run-walk, then short continuous runs every other day, each gated on 0/10 during and the next morning. Your HRV baseline has also slid from ~36 to ~32 over the week with almost no load, which is one more reason not to push. Manchester is 21 weeks away; the plan can absorb three more weeks of bike far better than a strain that keeps recurring through December. Her view outranks this plan — if she says differently, tell me and I will rewrite it.
